correctness.rationale: The exact quadratic finite-difference expansion yields error h/2 times the frame Rayleigh diagonal. Its squared norm gives the loss exactly. Cauchy--Schwarz and orthogonal Frobenius invariance yield sharp min/max; the recursive mean-Rayleigh construction proves attainment without assuming positive curvature. Sphere fourth moments prove the Haar risk and the uniform sign symmetry proves unbiasedness. For any randomized frame distribution, Haar averaging over an adversarial curvature orientation yields a universal minimax lower bound, attained by Haar frames. Symmetric signed probes prove the stated C^3 bias bound. Exact rational and symbolic cases, 900 numerical identities/inequalities and 54,000 Haar-frame moment samples were independently replayed from the delivered verify.py; they are corroboration, not proofs of infinite claims.

value.rationale: The 2026 k+1-evaluation one-sided projected-gradient estimator has a basis-selection ambiguity with a sharp quantitative effect: a rank-one PSD Hessian incurs k times as much squared error in an eigenframe as in a balanced frame, while trace-zero indefinite compressed curvature admits exact finite-step differentiation. When eigendirections are unknown, Haar sampling is provably minimax with an explicit curvature-spectrum risk, rather than merely an arbitrary random basis. This is a natural and actionable design fact for a concrete numerical differentiation primitive and remains meaningful without an end-to-end optimizer theorem. Unlike a textbook diagonalization identity alone, it resolves the sampling-design decision under an explicit information constraint.
